mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above the prior month's level precedes a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to tightened discount rates affecting expected future cash flows.
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative when FEDFUNDS crosses the threshold upward.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 5% for two consecutive months, labor market slack increases, reducing equity risk premia and driving positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: In 100+ test windows, no significant positive return (t-test p > 0.05) when UNRATE crosses below 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in HOUST (units of housing starts) followed by a rebound above the prior low predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals a bottom in construction demand and broader economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < min(HOUST[t-3], HOUST[t-6]) and HOUST[t+1] > min(HOUST[t-3], HOUST[t-6])
failure_condition: Over 200 windows, no statistically significant positive 60-day returns after such bottoms (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in INDPRO (industrial production) exceeding -2% for three months indicate supply-side weakness, which is associated with negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns as investors anticipate slower growth.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < INDPRO[t-1] by >-2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: In 50 such contraction periods, 20-day returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in CPIAUCSL (CPI) followed by a sustained rise above the prior level triggers a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as expectations for future inflation normalization boost equity valuations.
failure_condition: Over 100 such events, no positive 5-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When PAYEMS (employment) rises by more than 50,000 jobs in a single month, it indicates labor market strength and supports a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return via higher wage growth expectations.
failure_condition: In 100 such months, no significant positive 20-day returns (Granger causality rejected).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 2% in the same month suggests dual demand weakness, which is associated with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return due to reduced economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < GDPC1[t-1] by >-2% AND RSAFS < RSAFS[t-1] by >-2%
failure_condition: In 30 such events, 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of GDPC1 (GDP) exceeds its 12-month high by at least 1%, it signals an over-supplied economy and predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate slower growth.
failure_condition: Over 40 such windows, forward returns remain non-negative (p > 0.05).
